rundown: Oilers beat Rangers 3-1 at Rogers Place in Edmonton in front of 17,047. Oilers led 2-1 after two periods and never looked back.
4 goals in all. Oilers's last: Leon Draisaitl Goal Wrist Shot, assists: none, 3rd period 18:47.
Leading the way — Rangers: Jaroslav Chmelar 1 goal, 1 pts; Mika Zibanejad 1 ast. Oilers: Leon Draisaitl 2 goals, 2 pts; Mattias Ekholm 1 ast.
Where Oilers won it: they out-hit them 23-19.
Against the closing line (DraftKings): Oilers closed as 1.5-goal favorites and covered by 0.5; the total closed at 6.5 and they combined for 4, under by 2.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 9, 7:55 PM ET. It had Rangers 44% and Oilers 56%, projecting Rangers 2.9 – Oilers 3.3 (6.2 total, Oilers by 0.4).

Final: Rangers 1 – Oilers 3. Right winner: it had Oilers at 56%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Rangers came in with a 3% below average attack and a 3% stingier than average defense (10-7-1, 3.1 scored and 2.9 allowed a game over 18 games), worth about 77 and 77 games of evidence. Projected to score 2.9, they scored 1 (−1.9 goals, 66% under); projected to allow 3.3, they allowed 3 (−0.3 goals, 9% under).

Oilers came in with a 9% above average attack and a league-average defense (12-3-3, 4.2 scored and 3.1 allowed a game over 18 games), worth about 77 and 77 games of evidence. Projected to score 3.3, they scored 3 (−0.3 goals, 9% under); projected to allow 2.9, they allowed 1 (−1.9 goals, 66% under).

The bigger miss was Rangers' scoring (-1.9 goals against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 4 against 6.2 projected (-2.2), about the 19th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±2.5).

Margin: Oilers by 2 against Oilers by 0.4 projected, about the 75th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±2.5).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body:

NYR +1.5 (-185) at -185: the algo gave it 64% vs 62% fair (+2.2 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. OVER 6.5 (-112) at -112: the algo gave it 49% vs 50% fair (-1.8 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. UNDER 6.5 (-108) at -108: the algo gave it 51% vs 50% fair (+1.8 pts) — won (+0.9u); same number as the close.

The line barely moved between the algo's snapshot and the close.

No bet: nothing cleared the algo's bar before the game.

review.title: Where the public and the money were
review.body:
Splits (Action Network + DraftKings): spread: 29% of bets on Rangers, 3% of the money — Oilers covered; total: 59% of bets on the over, 87% of the money — it went under; moneyline: 7% of bets on Rangers, 2% of the money.

The sharp side by the algo's read was Oilers, who won and covered.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.658 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +1.7 goals. It counts toward NHL scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 38 graded NHL games the algo now scales scoring ×0.977 and gives home teams +0.1 goals. Team corrections so far: Rangers attack ×0.967, defense ×0.989 (3 games); Oilers attack ×1.001, defense ×0.961 (3 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
